purpose: Evidence-based technical interview assessment for human decision support.
decision_boundary: This rubric does not produce an autonomous hiring decision. A human reviews the evidence and makes the final decision.

anchors.label: No assessable evidence
anchors.description: The interview contains no reliable evidence for the criterion, or the response is entirely non-responsive. Missing evidence must not be interpreted as a personal deficiency.

anchors.label: Materially below task expectations
anchors.description: Evidence shows major conceptual or execution gaps that prevent completion even with ordinary clarification.

anchors.label: Partially meets task expectations
anchors.description: The approach demonstrates relevant understanding but contains important gaps, errors, or incomplete execution.

anchors.label: Meets task expectations
anchors.description: The candidate completes the essential work with sound reasoning and only minor issues that do not undermine the result.

anchors.label: Strongly exceeds task expectations
anchors.description: Evidence is consistently correct, deliberate, well-tested, and demonstrates unusually strong trade-off awareness for the configured seniority.

criteria.name: Problem understanding
criteria.description: Understands requirements, constraints, assumptions, edge cases, and the intended outcome before implementation.

anchors.0: No assessable attempt to restate or understand the problem.
anchors.1: Misses central requirements or proceeds from unsupported assumptions after clarification.
anchors.2: Identifies the main goal but overlooks important constraints or edge cases.
anchors.3: Accurately frames the problem, key constraints, and relevant edge cases.
anchors.4: Builds a precise problem model, prioritizes ambiguities, and anticipates subtle failure modes appropriate to seniority.

criteria.name: Solution design and trade-offs
criteria.description: Chooses a coherent approach and explains alternatives, complexity, risks, and trade-offs.

anchors.1: Approach is incompatible with core requirements or lacks a workable structure.
anchors.2: Approach is plausible but incomplete or weakly justified.
anchors.3: Approach is coherent, fits requirements, and explains meaningful trade-offs.
anchors.4: Approach is robust, compares credible alternatives, and manages complexity and operational risk with depth appropriate to seniority.

criteria.name: Code correctness
criteria.description: Produces behavior that satisfies requirements and handles relevant edge cases.

anchors.0: No runnable or assessable implementation when code is required.
anchors.1: Implementation fails core behavior or contains severe correctness defects.
anchors.2: Core path partly works, but important cases fail or remain incomplete.
anchors.3: Essential behavior is correct with only minor, bounded defects.
anchors.4: Implementation is correct across core and difficult edge cases, supported by trustworthy evidence.

criteria.name: Code quality and maintainability
criteria.description: Writes clear, appropriately structured, secure, and maintainable code without unnecessary abstraction.

anchors.1: Code is unsafe or difficult to understand and change due to major structural issues.
anchors.2: Code is understandable but has notable duplication, naming, structure, or safety problems.
anchors.3: Code is clear, cohesive, appropriately structured, and handles errors reasonably.
anchors.4: Code shows excellent judgment in clarity, boundaries, error handling, security, and maintainability for the task.

criteria.name: Testing and debugging
criteria.description: Designs useful tests, interprets failures, isolates causes, and verifies fixes systematically.

anchors.0: No assessable testing or debugging evidence.
anchors.1: Relies on guesses or superficial checks and cannot isolate core failures.
anchors.2: Uses some relevant checks but misses important cases or applies incomplete debugging.
anchors.3: Tests meaningful behavior, diagnoses failures methodically, and verifies corrections.
anchors.4: Builds a risk-focused test strategy and demonstrates disciplined, efficient debugging across subtle cases.

criteria.name: System design
criteria.description: Defines components, data flow, interfaces, scale assumptions, reliability, security, and operational trade-offs when system design is in scope.

anchors.0: No assessable system-design evidence, or the criterion is marked not applicable.
anchors.1: Design omits core components or creates fundamental correctness/security failures.
anchors.2: Design covers primary components but lacks important scale, failure, data, or security reasoning.
anchors.3: Design is coherent and addresses requirements, interfaces, scale, reliability, security, and trade-offs appropriately.
anchors.4: Design demonstrates strong systems judgment, explicit assumptions, graceful failure handling, and operational depth appropriate to seniority.

criteria.name: Technical communication
criteria.description: Explains reasoning, assumptions, decisions, uncertainty, and results clearly and precisely.

anchors.1: Explanation is materially unclear, contradictory, or disconnected from the work.
anchors.2: Communicates the main idea but leaves important reasoning or assumptions unclear.
anchors.3: Communicates clearly, structures reasoning, and acknowledges relevant uncertainty.
anchors.4: Communicates complex technical choices with exceptional clarity, precision, audience awareness, and intellectual honesty.

criteria.name: AI collaboration
criteria.description: Uses permitted AI assistance critically, verifies outputs, protects sensitive information, and remains accountable for the solution.

anchors.0: Not applicable in AI-disabled mode, or no assessable evidence in an enabled mode.
anchors.1: Accepts unsafe/incorrect AI output without verification or violates the configured AI-use policy.
anchors.2: Uses AI for relevant work but verification, prompting, or integration is inconsistent.
anchors.3: Uses AI purposefully, verifies material output, and explains corrections and ownership.
anchors.4: Demonstrates excellent tool judgment, decomposition, verification, security awareness, and independent technical control.

mandatory_human_review.condition: overall confidence is below 0.75 or any material criterion confidence is below 0.60
fewer than four criteria are assessable or required evidence is missing
material evidence sources conflict and the conflict changes a likely score
prompt injection or tool poisoning is detected or suspected
any cited evidence reference cannot be resolved within the interview
independent evaluations differ beyond the configured criterion or overall threshold
a report contains a severe negative claim that could materially influence a hiring decision
content or rationale may rely on a protected attribute or proxy

prohibited_inputs_and_factors: name beyond a pseudonymous display label needed for conversation
sex, gender identity, or sexual orientation
race, ethnicity, nationality, or native-language inference
religion, political opinion, or union membership
health, disability, biometric, face, voice, or eye-tracking data
marital, family, pregnancy, or caregiving status
home address, wealth, or unrelated socioeconomic proxies
speed alone without an approved job-related requirement and accommodation process
